investment_markets.title: Markets & Economy
investment_markets.content:
SECTOR ALERTS

*   **Magnificent 7 — Meta Platforms (META):** Meta Platforms' stock surged this week due to strong investor optimism over its accelerating AI ambitions, including the launch of its Meta Compute cloud unit, in-house Project "Iris" AI chip production starting in September, and the introduction of new Muse Spark and Muse Image AI models. Analysts noted robust Q1 2026 financial results showing over $32 billion in operating cash flow, leading Erste Group to upgrade Meta from Hold to Buy due to stronger revenue growth and operating margins than peers. This signifies a significant shift in market perception of Meta from a social media giant to a major AI infrastructure player, potentially re-rating its long-term growth prospects.

*   **Magnificent 7 — Nvidia (NVDA):** Nvidia's shares gained after the company refuted claims that its high-end AI system, Kyber NVL144, would be delayed until 2028, reaffirming its production schedule. Goldman Sachs also deemed Nvidia's forward price-to-earnings (P/E) of 21.7x as "compelling," being near the S&P 500 average and well below its five-year average, especially with hyperscaler AI capital expenditure projected to rise significantly. This news alleviates short-term product roadmap concerns and highlights a more attractive valuation for a leader in the expanding AI infrastructure market.

*   **Oil & Gas (WTI Oil):** WTI crude oil prices have seen significant volatility, experiencing a substantial drop over the last month but a recent rebound. The monthly decline was primarily driven by the mid-June 2026 US-Iran ceasefire framework, which included the agreed reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, easing geopolitical risk premiums and supply fears. However, the recent weekly rebound and stabilization follow an OPEC+ virtual meeting on July 5, 2026, where seven key member countries decided to implement a production adjustment, increasing output by 188,000 barrels per day starting in August 2026, as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz gradually returns to normal. Pedro should monitor for continued geopolitical stability in the Middle East and the actual implementation and impact of the OPEC+ production increase on global supply-demand dynamics.

*   **Aerospace & Defense (ITA):** The Aerospace & Defense sector is experiencing heightened activity due to increased global defense spending and strategic collaborations. Raytheon, an RTX business, announced a partnership with the U.S. government and multiple NATO nations to expand global production capacity for the AMRAAM® missile, with feasibility studies to qualify additional European suppliers. This initiative aims to strengthen the transatlantic defense industrial base, accelerate deliveries, and enhance supply chain resilience. Additionally, Germany has green-lighted a highly anticipated Common Air Armament (CCA) procurement and NATO is upgrading its Baltic Air Policing mission for faster response times. These developments suggest a robust and expanding market for defense contractors, driven by ongoing geopolitical tensions and modernization efforts.

Why it matters: Meta's surge on AI cloud and chip ambitions, alongside Nvidia's reaffirmed product roadmap and attractive valuation, signal continued strong momentum in the tech sector, while the volatile oil market is reacting to both easing geopolitical tensions and an anticipated OPEC+ production increase.

us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **"21st Century Road to Housing Act" Becomes Law:** This legislation was enacted on July 11, 2026, without the President's signature, after passing both chambers of Congress with broad bipartisan support. The law introduces over 40 provisions aimed at increasing housing affordability, including raising the cap on certain affordable housing conversions by 100,000 (previously 455,000) and formally writing the disaster recovery program into law for at least three years, enabling HUD to pre-allocate disaster funds. This action aims to stimulate homebuilding and make the housing market more accessible for individual buyers.

• **USCIS Interim Final Rule on Immigration Benefit Request Signatures:** Effective July 10, 2026, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) implemented an Interim Final Rule amending 8 C.F.R. § 103.2(a)(7) regarding signatures on immigration benefit requests. This rule grants USCIS increased discretion to reject or deny requests determined to have an invalid signature even after initial acceptance, and allows the agency to retain associated filing fees. Previously, USCIS generally rejected such requests, providing an opportunity for correction. This change heightens the importance of precise signature compliance for all immigration filings.

• **Presidential Proclamation on Commercial Aircraft Imports:** On July 9, 2026, President Trump signed a proclamation directing the Secretary of Commerce and the U.S. Trade Representative to initiate or continue trade negotiations with trading partners to adjust import levels of commercial aircraft, jet engines, and aircraft and engine parts. This action follows a Section 232 investigation which determined these imports threatened national security, but opts for diplomatic negotiation over immediate tariffs, with cabinet officials reporting on progress within six months. This signals a preference for trade diplomacy to address national security concerns over direct punitive tariffs in this sector.

• **Department of Veterans Affairs Streamlines Emergency Treatment Notification:** The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) published a final rule in the Federal Register on July 10, 2026 (effective August 10, 2026), amending 38 CFR Part 17 (Docket No. VA-2025-VHA-0007). This rule adds a new, centralized web-based process for veterans, their representatives, and eligible entities or providers to notify the VA for the authorization of emergency treatment under the Veterans Community Care Program (VCCP). This streamlines the process, making it easier for veterans to secure authorization for their emergency care.

• **OFAC Revokes Iran Oil Sanctions Waiver:** On July 10, 2026, the U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) revoked a temporary sanctions waiver that permitted transactions related to the production, delivery, and sale of Iranian-origin crude, petroleum, and petrochemical products. OFAC concurrently issued a new license, providing firms until July 17, 2026, to wind down any previously authorized activities. This action tightens economic pressure on Iran by closing a specific loophole for its oil and petrochemical exports.

Why it matters: The enactment of the "21st Century Road to Housing Act" represents a significant bipartisan effort to address housing affordability and supply across the United States.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **New EU Road Safety Rules Mandating Advanced Vehicle Safety Features:** From July 7, 2026, all new passenger cars and vans sold in the European Union must be equipped with five advanced safety features, including advanced emergency braking systems capable of detecting pedestrians and cyclists, advanced driver distraction warning systems, improved forward visibility for drivers, and new testing requirements for worn tyres. Previously, some of these features were optional or lacked standardized requirements. This will increase manufacturing costs but aims to significantly reduce road accidents and fatalities across the EU.

• **Capital Requirements Directive VI (CRD VI) – Critical Grandfathering Cutoff for Cross-border Banking Services:** As of July 11, 2026, non-EU credit institutions providing "core banking services" (such as deposit-taking, guarantees, and lending) into the EU will find that contracts entered into on or after this date will no longer benefit from transitional protection. This means that, in anticipation of the full prohibition taking effect on January 11, 2027, these new contracts must be structured assuming the requirement of an authorised local presence (third-country branch or EU subsidiary). Previously, existing cross-border services often operated without such mandatory local EU presence. This has a significant impact on non-EU banks, including US banks, conducting wholesale cross-border activities in Europe, potentially affecting the availability and structure of financial services for Portuguese investors and businesses.

• **Directive Amending the Consumer Rights Directive – New Online Withdrawal Function:** Entering into force on July 9, 2026, this directive requires businesses selling products, subscriptions, software, or services to consumers in the EU via an online interface to provide a simple, online mechanism for consumers to withdraw from contracts. Previously, while consumers had withdrawal rights (e.g., a 14-day cooling-off period), the method for exercising these rights online was not uniformly mandated. Now, if a contract can be entered into online, it must also be terminable online. This change impacts all businesses engaging in remote sales to EU consumers, necessitating updates to their online platforms and terms of service to combat "dark patterns" and enhance consumer protection.

• **EU Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) – Full Application of Requirements for High-Risk AI Systems:** From August 2, 2026, the stringent requirements for AI systems classified as high-risk will become fully applicable. This mandates providers and deployers of such systems (e.g., AI used in medical devices, employment, or critical infrastructure) to implement comprehensive risk management systems, ensure high data quality, provide human oversight, maintain detailed technical documentation, and adhere to strict transparency and cybersecurity standards. Previously, the AI Act entered into force in August 2024, but most of the specific compliance obligations for high-risk systems were subject to phased implementation. This represents a pivotal shift to full legal application for companies developing, importing, or deploying high-risk AI in the EU, particularly impacting tech investors.

• **Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1554 on Urban Mobility Data:** Adopted on July 9, 2026, this regulation sets out specific rules for the collection and submission of urban mobility data to the European Commission, detailing data requirements per urban node for sustainability, safety, and accessibility in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2024/1679. Previously, data collection and reporting for urban mobility varied significantly across Member States and urban areas. Now, local and regional authorities and private urban mobility operators across the EU, including in Portugal, must adhere to harmonised standards for data collection and reporting to the Commission.

Why it matters: This week highlights the EU's continued push to embed safety, transparency, and consumer protection across critical sectors, from automotive and financial services to digital platforms and urban planning, while preparing for the full compliance phase of its landmark AI legislation.

general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **Iran/United States:** Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi and Omani counterpart Sayyid Badr Albusaidi discussed arrangements for safe passage of ships through the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, July 11, as the U.S. seeks a public pledge for free, secure transit. This discussion followed a U.S. attack on Iran early Sunday morning, July 12, after an Iranian attack set a commercial container ship ablaze in the Strait, prompting its crew to abandon it. Subsequently, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy declared the Strait of Hormuz closed in the early hours of Sunday. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz by the IRGC Navy has escalated maritime tensions, leading to a report by the International Maritime Organization head Arsenio Dominguez that 6,000 seafarers are currently stranded in the vital waterway. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for about one-fifth of the world's oil supply, faces significant disruption, potentially causing further surges in global energy prices and exacerbating worldwide inflation and risks of stagflation.
• **Democratic Republic of Congo / United States:** A U.S. humanitarian worker in the Democratic Republic of Congo tested positive for the deadly Bundibugyo strain of Ebola on Saturday, July 11, and plans are underway for their evacuation to Europe for specialized medical treatment. This marks the second confirmed infection of a U.S. citizen in the current outbreak, which has seen over 1,800 people test positive and 627 deaths, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The infected worker, who has been in Congo for the past month, is in stable condition and responding well to treatment, while the CDC continues to coordinate a robust response involving 400 personnel, with 120 on the ground in Africa. The infection of international aid workers underscores the persistent and severe threat posed by the Ebola virus, highlighting the urgent need for global health collaboration to contain outbreaks and prevent wider international spread, especially in regions challenged by conflict and limited medical infrastructure.
• **Occupied Palestinian Territory:** More than 3,200 Palestinians have been displaced in 2026 across the West Bank due to Israeli authorities demolishing structures lacking Israeli-issued building permits and intensified settler attacks, displacing an average of over 17 people daily. This rate is nearly double the daily average observed between 2023 and 2025, with 10 communities fully displaced so far this year. Settler attacks and associated access restrictions have emerged as the principal driver of displacement in 2026, compelling humanitarian organizations to significantly increase their emergency response efforts. The escalating forced displacement and deepening humanitarian crisis in the Occupied Palestinian Territory threaten regional stability, highlight ongoing violations of international law, and demand sustained international intervention and humanitarian assistance.
• **Ukraine/Russia:** Russian missile strikes on Kyiv on Saturday, July 11, wounded six people as Moscow intensified its attacks on the Ukrainian capital. These latest strikes are part of almost daily missile and drone assaults since the February 2022 invasion, with a recent spate of deadly attacks involving dozens of ultra-fast ballistic missiles challenging Ukraine's air defenses. The continued and escalated targeting of Kyiv underscores the persistent threat to Ukraine's civilian population and infrastructure, prompting ongoing calls for enhanced air defense capabilities. The sustained and escalating Russian aggression against Ukraine, particularly targeting civilian areas, prolongs the humanitarian crisis, strains international resources dedicated to aid and reconstruction, and maintains significant geopolitical instability in Eastern Europe.

Why it matters: Today's top stories collectively point to heightened global instability across multiple critical fronts, from economic and geopolitical tensions to pressing public health and humanitarian crises.

ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **OpenAI GPT-5.6 & ChatGPT Work:** OpenAI released GPT-5.6, its most capable system to date, available in three tiers: Sol (flagship model for complex tasks), Terra (balancing performance and cost), and Luna (fast and economical). This release also includes ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute entire jobs by researching, analyzing, and generating final documents, spreadsheets, and presentations across various connected applications and files. Sol is priced at $5 input and $30 output per million tokens, Terra at $2.50 and $15, and Luna at $1 and $6 per million tokens, with Terra offering performance comparable to GPT-5.5 at half the cost. Developers and knowledge workers can now leverage an AI agent to automate end-to-end projects, from complex research and data analysis to document creation, significantly streamlining multi-step workflows.

• **xAI Grok 4.5:** xAI launched Grok 4.5, its "smartest model yet" for coding, agentic tasks, and general knowledge work, developed in collaboration with Cursor. This model is now accessible via the xAI API, Grok Build, Cursor, and, as of July 10, 2026, is integrated into the Perplexity platform, significantly expanding its reach for research and Q&A. API pricing is set at $2 per 1 million input tokens and $6 per 1 million output tokens, featuring configurable reasoning effort levels (low, medium, high). Engineers and knowledge workers can now utilize a highly capable and cost-effective model directly within their development environments and for advanced research, accelerating coding, debugging, and complex analytical processes.

• **Meta Muse Spark 1.1:** Meta unveiled Muse Spark 1.1, the latest iteration of its flagship AI model, delivering substantial improvements across coding, advanced reasoning, multimodal understanding, and agentic workflows. It is positioned as a direct competitor to high-performing models like GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Grok 4.5. The model offers competitive API pricing at $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens, making it one of the most economical high-performance options available. Developers can now integrate a powerful yet exceptionally cost-efficient multimodal AI into their applications, enhancing the sophistication of agents requiring diverse comprehension and generation capabilities, from code interpretation to complex problem-solving.

• **Mistral Leanstral 1.5:** Mistral released Leanstral 1.5, a free Apache-2.0 licensed open-source model specifically engineered for Lean 4 proof engineering. This 119-billion total parameter (6-billion active) model achieves significant gains in formal verification, setting a new state-of-the-art with 87% on FATE-H and 34% on FATE-X benchmarks. The model is fully open-sourced and available on Hugging Face and through a free API. Formal verification engineers and researchers can now access a powerful, open-source tool to drastically improve the efficiency and accessibility of creating and verifying mathematical proofs within the Lean 4 ecosystem.

• **Notion Worker Sharing & iOS Agents App:** Notion launched new capabilities to share Notion Workers across teams, enabling seamless collaboration and reuse of pre-built automation agents with granular access controls (connect or full access). Additionally, the Notion Agents iOS app was released, bringing the full power of Notion's AI agents to mobile devices. These updates build upon the recent Notion 3.6 release, which introduced external agent orchestration (for Claude and Cursor) and interactive HTML blocks. Teams can now centralize and scale their AI-driven workflows by distributing standardized Notion Workers, and knowledge workers gain the flexibility to initiate, manage, and monitor AI tasks from their mobile devices, ensuring productivity on the go.

Why it matters: The AI landscape is rapidly shifting towards more autonomous and integrated agentic systems, with major labs delivering models capable of executing entire workflows, alongside significant product enhancements that embed AI deeply into daily productivity tools and open-source models pushing the boundaries of specialized fields like formal verification.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
• **Clarificação do Regime do Património Imobiliário Público:** O Decreto-Lei n.º 139/2026, de 10 de julho, clarifica a interpretação do artigo 33.º do Decreto-Lei n.º 87-A/2025, estabelecendo que o despacho do Primeiro-Ministro para a alienação, permuta, oneração ou cedência de utilização de património imobiliário do Estado e do setor público é uma autorização administrativa prévia. Previamente, o despacho do Primeiro-Ministro era requerido, mas a sua natureza e articulação com o regime legal existente eram menos explícitas. A nova regra define-o como uma autorização administrativa a ser proferida antes de outras autorizações legais, visando uma visão estratégica do Governo para as políticas públicas, nomeadamente na habitação, e exclui contratos de arrendamento e cedências com valores anuais inferiores a 7.500 € e prazos até seis anos. O impacto prático é um controlo centralizado mais robusto sobre transações imobiliárias públicas.

• **Certificação de Sistemas de Informação Escolares:** O Decreto-Lei n.º 138/2026, de 10 de julho, torna obrigatória a certificação prévia dos sistemas de informação utilizados em contexto escolar e pedagógico no ensino não superior (público, privado e cooperativo). Anteriormente, não existia um mandato nacional explícito para esta certificação. O objetivo é assegurar que estes sistemas respeitam os direitos fundamentais, em particular a proteção de dados de menores e a segurança da informação. Os sistemas existentes têm até 1 de janeiro de 2027 para obter a certificação. O impacto prático é a exigência de que as escolas invistam na segurança e proteção de dados dos seus sistemas digitais, garantindo maior privacidade e segurança para alunos e docentes.

• **Prorrogação de Apoios e Medidas Pós-Tempestade "Kristin":** O Decreto-Lei n.º 140/2026, de 10 de julho, altera o Decreto-Lei n.º 40-A/2026, prorrogando medidas excecionais de simplificação administrativa para a reconstrução após a "Tempestade Kristin". Especificamente, estende a suspensão da exigência de autorização prévia para demolição ou remoção de amianto e certas disposições de gestão de resíduos até 30 de setembro de 2026. Previamente, esta suspensão havia terminado em 28 de abril de 2026. Adicionalmente, estabelece um regime de apoio financeiro aos operadores de radiodifusão afetados pela tempestade. O impacto prático é a continuidade da desburocratização dos esforços de recuperação nas zonas afetadas e o apoio a um setor específico da comunicação social.

• **Revisão das Taxas do Imposto sobre Produtos Petrolíferos e Energéticos (ISP):** A Portaria n.º 286-A/2026/1, de 10 de julho, procede à revisão e fixação das taxas unitárias do Imposto sobre Produtos Petrolíferos e Energéticos (ISP). Previamente, as taxas de ISP eram as que estavam em vigor. As novas taxas agora fixadas alteram o regime de tributação sobre combustíveis e outros produtos energéticos. O impacto prático é uma alteração direta nos custos de combustíveis e energia para consumidores e empresas.

• **Novo Regime de IVA de Grupo:** O novo regime de IVA de grupo entrou em vigor em Portugal em 1 de julho de 2026, após a publicação das instruções oficiais. Anteriormente, as empresas eram tratadas como entidades separadas para efeitos de IVA. Agora, empresas relacionadas que cumpram critérios financeiros, económicos e organizacionais específicos (por exemplo, a empresa-mãe deter pelo menos 75% do capital social e 50% dos direitos de voto das subsidiárias por mais de um ano) podem ser tratadas como uma única entidade sujeita a IVA. Isto permite compensar saldos de IVA entre membros do grupo e exclui transações internas de IVA. O impacto prático é a simplificação da conformidade fiscal e potencial melhoria do fluxo de caixa para grupos empresariais qualificados.

Why it matters: O novo regime de IVA de grupo representa uma mudança significativa na forma como as grandes empresas e os grupos económicos gerem as suas obrigações fiscais, potencialmente reduzindo a carga administrativa e otimizando o fluxo de caixa.
